walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Investigative Study of a Religious Practice — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Investigative Study of a Religious Practice brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Investigative Study of a Religious Practice.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1902 Gifford Lectures examined mystical experience?
options: William James
Rudolf Otto
Friedrich Schleiermacher
Mircea Eliade

mcqs.q: Which 16th-century Spanish mystic wrote Interior Castle?
options: John of the Cross
Teresa of Avila
Ignatius Loyola
Francisco Suarez

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The Buddha created the universe.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.
The Buddha created the universe.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
